confirmed: S1-O1 (creative quality) and S1-O2 (novelty) are scored on the one image each participant submitted per condition. The same two senior product-design experts rated them, blind to group and condition, and each design's score is the mean of the two experts' ratings. Neither is a self-report (p. 7, Sects. 3.3, 3.4, 3.4.2: 'the final score for each design was the mean of the two expert ratings'; p. 8, Table 2; p. 9, Sect. 4.1).

S1-O3 is computed from the two experts' categorical coding of each submitted image on four attributes, so it is scored on the output. Table 2 names the evaluator as 'expert classification; categorical coding', which makes category_count the closest measure code (p. 8, Sect. 3.4.4, Tables 1 and 2; p. 9, Sect. 4.1: 'creative diversity indices calculated from expert classifications').

The diversity formula is announced but not printed. The PDF page holds no image, and no text sits between 'four attribute-level measures:' and 'In the creative diversity formula, V1, V2, V3, and V4' (p. 8, Sect. 3.4.4, right column).

S1-O3 construct 'other' and question 'with_ai' follow the codebook. The score measures attribute breadth within one image, not variation across people or across one person's ideas, so it is neither diversity nor flexibility (p. 8, Sect. 3.4.4: 'the unit of classification and analysis was the individual submitted image'; p. 16, Sect. 5: 'reflects feature breadth within a single concept, not variation across a full set of outputs').

AI was available when every scored image was produced. In all four conditions participants generated concepts with the assigned image generator and submitted one of its outputs, and no condition works without AI. With non-diversity constructs, question with_ai is correct for S1-O1 to S1-O3, and timing is immediate (p. 7, Sect. 3.3).

S1-O1 construct usefulness matches the codebook's 'quality of a single output'. Its items are functional completeness, aesthetic/formal quality, technical feasibility, user orientation, and overall completeness. The S1-O2 novelty items rate departure from conventional approaches and breakthroughs in form, structure, or interaction (p. 7, Sects. 3.4.2 and 3.4.3; p. 8, Table 2).

Unit 'output' fits S1-O1 to S1-O3. Each participant submitted exactly four images, one per condition, and each score belongs to one design. Quality and novelty enter a mixed repeated-measures ANOVA with four image scores per participant (error df 54). Diversity is analysed per image by ART (df 162) (p. 7, Sect. 3.3; p. 8, Sect. 3.4.4; p. 12, Table 5; p. 14, Table 6 and Sect. 4.5; p. 15, Table 7).
n_units null follows form-spec rule 1. The paper gives 60 participants and four images each but never prints the image total (p. 5, Sect. 3.1; p. 7, Sect. 3.3).

S1-O4 (perceived usefulness) is a participant questionnaire completed after all four tasks. The form codes it scored_on_output false, measure self_report, and question none, which the form-spec allows for an outcome that answers none of the three questions (p. 7, Sects. 3.3 and 3.4.1; p. 8, Table 2).

Table 6 matches S1-O2: IGAS F(1, 54) = 9.916, p = 0.003, 0.155. PT 2.287, p = 0.136, 0.041. IGAS x PT 0.545, p = 0.464. Post hoc IGAS0 > IGAS1 0.444 (SE 0.141, [0.161, 0.726]), 0.44 in the text. No PT post hoc is printed (p. 14, Table 6; p. 13, Sect. 4.4).

Table 7 and Sect. 4.5 match S1-O3: IGAS F(1, 162) = 40.80, p < .001, t(162) = 4.82. PT F 0.209 (text 0.21), p = 0.648, t(162) = 0.46. IGAS x PT p = 0.727. The table note says ART gives no error df, mean squares, or effect size (p. 14, Sect. 4.5; p. 15, Table 7).

Fig. 5 labels, read from a zoomed render because the text layer lacks them: ChatGPT-4o concrete 3.34, abstract 2.88; Midjourney V6 3.59 and 3.57, overlapping. Abstract = 3.57 fits the printed 0.688 simple effect, and the four cells reproduce the Table 3 margins 3.58, 3.11, and 3.23 (p. 13, Fig. 5).
Reliability values in measure_detail match: Cronbach alpha 0.840, 0.847, 0.787. ICC(3,2) is 0.703 [0.664, 0.737] for quality and 0.632 [0.561, 0.692] for novelty (p. 9, Sect. 4.1).

Directions match: Midjourney V6 is higher on quality, novelty, and diversity. Abstract prompts are lower on quality and usefulness, with no clear difference on novelty (p = 0.136) or diversity (p = 0.648) (pp. 9, 11, 12, 14, 15).

No outcome that bears on the three questions is missing. The paper reports no count of concepts generated, no comparison across people, and no work after AI is removed. The 5-minute interviews report no scored results, and EXP and ATP are classified groups that the form keeps in notes (p. 5, Sect. 3.1; p. 7, Sect. 3.3; pp. 9 to 15, Sects. 4.1 to 4.5).
summary: The form codes c135's outcomes correctly: creative quality and novelty are blind expert ratings of the one AI-generated image each participant submitted per condition, the image-level 'creative diversity' score is rightly coded other and with_ai because it measures attribute breadth within one image, and perceived usefulness is correctly marked as a self-report. Every number in the 'reported' fields matches Tables 3 to 7 and Fig. 5, no outcome that bears on the three questions is missing, and criterion 3 holds.
